rows.what the ink shows: The initial descending p, reduced r and acute accent are visible; the middle letters run into a low connected stroke. At the right a tall looped stroke is followed by a separate rounded e-like glyph, leaving the terminal t/e sequence unresolved.
A heavy rising horizontal cancellation covers almost the full word; only a short dark left hook and low central remnants remain, insufficient to separate letters.
The small initial open curved stroke is followed by a low angular a and an extended horizontal r ending; there is no tall stem within the word.
An open e and crossed x precede short upright strokes; the reduced middle continues into a long low run, then a dotted i and clearly crossed final t.

The underlined baseline form begins with a compact s and has tightly joined tall strokes for the contracted t/b/l group, ending in an open e; no separate a appears. The thinner inserted stable sits above it.

The large initial M and following e-like loop are clear, followed by a small horizontal stroke and tall h-like stroke. A distinct dot and low terminal loop make an abbreviated Méth. form a concrete competitor to full Méthode; the thin méthode above does not settle the original baseline letters.

Above the baseline L are three separate components: a curved left parenthesis, a capped descending 2, and a curved right parenthesis. The central numeral matches the small unparenthesized 2 over L in the next line.
